subject.title: Feature: Silence Watchdog + Response Delivery Confirmation — runtime-enforced operator visibility

question: Should this umbrella remain the canonical product direction for default runtime operator-visibility guarantees, or should maintainers split it into the existing narrower delivery-confirmation and watchdog issues?
rationale: The source shows missing pieces, but the permanent behavior changes channel-visible defaults, retry/alert policy, config shape, and cross-channel delivery contracts, so automation cannot safely choose the product boundary.

options.title: Split And Coordinate Existing Canonicals
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87561, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46830, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77771 as the implementation tracks while keeping this issue as an umbrella until the split is explicit.

options.title: Make This The Canonical Umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue as the single product owner for both subsystems and require narrower PRs to reference it as the umbrella acceptance contract.

options.title: Decline Default Runtime Messages
options.body: Close or narrow the feature if maintainers do not want default gateway-generated operator messages/retries beyond existing typing, heartbeat, and pending-final recovery.

recommendation.title: Split And Coordinate Existing Canonicals
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87561, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46830, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77771 as the implementation tracks while keeping this issue as an umbrella until the split is explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest source-history trail for reply dispatch, outbound delivery, typing lifecycle, and current main ownership points to steipete, with osolmaz owning a major overlapping product thread.
